mainTopic: A worker's wage claim, and the limits on taking a משכון from a borrower, even by a court agent
overview: The amud opens by finishing the משנה about a שכיר (hired worker) who swears and collects his wages. The גמרא explains why the בעל הבית's side is stronger: he has two חזקות and the worker has only one. It then works out what witnesses to the worker's demand must have seen, and how long that gives him to swear and collect. A new משנה follows about taking a משכון (collateral) from a borrower. The lender may do it only through בית דין, may not enter the borrower's house, and must give back things the borrower needs. In the גמרא, שמואל rules that a שליח בית דין may seize items outside but may not go into the house to take a משכון. The גמרא tests שמואל against the משנה, against פסוקים brought by רב יוסף, and against a ברייתא. That ברייתא seems to treat the court's agent like the borrower, and its answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Once payment is due, the employer pays attention and remembers
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its point: a busy בעל הבית might forget earlier, but when the payment deadline arrives he focuses and remembers.
steps.simpleTranslation: But once the time he must pay arrives, he takes it to heart and remembers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from just before this point. The employer is busy with his workers, but once the deadline to pay arrives, he concentrates and remembers whether he paid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא said the בעל הבית is busy with many workers and may get confused. Here it limits that claim. At the moment he is obligated to pay, he is careful not to violate בל תלין, so he remembers whether he paid. This is why the חזקה that a בעל הבית does not violate בל תלין still carries weight.

keyTerms.meaning: the time of his obligation (to pay)
he puts it on himself; he takes it to heart

phrases.english: But when the time of his obligation arrives –
he applies himself and remembers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the preceding answer from the earlier part of the daf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction in time: before the deadline versus at the deadline
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A busy employer cannot be relied on to remember whether he paid.
steps.terutzMaskana: At the deadline he concentrates and remembers, so his חזקה of not violating בל תלין stands.

steps.title: Isn't the worker also presumed not to steal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if we trust the בעל הבית not to violate בל תלין, we should equally trust the שכיר not to violate בל תגזול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And is the hired worker someone who violates 'do not steal'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a sharp question. Why give weight to the employer's חזקה when the worker also has a חזקה that he does not steal?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides could claim a presumption of honesty. The בעל הבית won't hold back wages (בל תלין), and the שכיר won't demand money he already got, which would be stealing (בל תגזול). So why should the employer's חזקה win and make the worker need a שבועה at all?

phrases.english: But is the hired worker suspected of violating the prohibition of 'do not steal'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי שָׂכִיר עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם בַּל תִּגְזֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reliance on the employer's חזקה described in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the בעל הבית's חזקה deserves extra weight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The worker has an equal חזקה of not stealing, so the two presumptions should cancel out.

steps.title: The employer has two presumptions, the worker only one
steps.stepSummary: The בעל הבית is backed by two חזקות: he doesn't violate בל תלין, and workers don't delay asking for wages. The שכיר has only one: he doesn't steal.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there are two presumptions; here, one presumption. For the employer there are two: one, that an employer doesn't violate 'do not hold back wages,' and one, that a worker doesn't delay asking for his wages. And here there is one presumption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the two sides are not equal. The employer has two presumptions supporting him and the worker has only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first חזקה is that the בעל הבית won't break בל תלין. The second is that a שכיר, who needs his money, won't wait to ask for it. So if the deadline came and went, he probably was already paid. Against these two, the worker has only his חזקה of not violating בל תגזול, so the employer's side is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: a legal presumption about how people normally act
the prohibition against holding back a worker's wages overnight

steps.whatToRemember: The בעל הבית has two חזקות (no בל תלין, and workers don't wait to ask), while the שכיר has only one (no בל תגזול). Two outweigh one.

phrases.english: There, there are two presumptions,
here, there is one presumption.

phrases.aramaic: גַּבֵּי בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אִיכָּא תְּרֵי חֲזָקֵי:
phrases.english: Concerning the employer there are two presumptions:

phrases.aramaic: חֲדָא דְּאֵין בַּעַל הַבַּיִת עוֹבֵר מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תָּלִין״,
phrases.english: one, that the employer does not violate the prohibition of 'do not hold back wages,'
and one, that a hired worker does not delay asking for his wages.
And here there is one presumption.
phrases.notes: The worker's one presumption is that he doesn't steal.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם תְּרֵי חֲזָקֵי הָכָא חֲדָא חֲזָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The worker's חזקה of not stealing balances the employer's חזקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The employer has two חזקות, which outweigh the worker's single one.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: witnesses that he demanded payment
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: if witnesses saw the worker demand his wages, he swears and collects, even after the deadline.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are witnesses that he demanded it from him, he swears and collects.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. This sets up the questions that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that after the deadline has passed, the worker can no longer swear and collect. This line gives an exception: if witnesses saw him demand payment, he can still swear and collect. The גמרא will now work out what exactly the witnesses must have seen.

keyTerms.meaning: that he demanded it from him

phrases.english: If there are witnesses that he demanded it from him –
he swears and collects.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With witnesses that the worker demanded payment, he swears and collects even after the deadline.

steps.title: Why witnesses? He is demanding it right in front of us
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why witnesses are needed to prove a demand when the worker is making his demand right now in court.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he is demanding it from him right in front of us!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what these witnesses add. We can all see the worker making his claim right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A demand in court is obvious, so witnesses to 'a demand' seem pointless. The question pushes the גמרא to explain that the witnesses must be testifying about something more specific.

keyTerms.meaning: he is demanding it from him

phrases.english: But he is demanding it from him in front of us?
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are how most printed copies read; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording, and both mean the same thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the משנה quoted in step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for witnesses in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The demand is happening openly in court, so witnesses to a demand add nothing.

steps.title: רבי אסי: the witnesses saw him demand it on time
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי explains that the witnesses testify the worker demanded payment during the proper time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: That he demanded it from him at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי answers that the witnesses aren't talking about today's demand. They saw him demand payment back during the proper time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A demand made during the payment window is what matters. It shows the worker did not just quietly wait, which weakens the חזקה that a worker doesn't delay asking for his wages.

keyTerms.meaning: at its proper time (the payment window)

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:
That he demanded it from him at its proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witnesses would only be proving the demand made in court now.
steps.terutzMaskana: The witnesses prove a demand made during the payment time.

steps.title: Maybe the employer paid afterward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: even if he demanded on time, maybe the employer paid him later.
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps afterward he paid him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אסי. One demand during the time doesn't prove the money was never paid after that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Seeing the worker demand once only proves that at that moment he hadn't been paid. The employer could have paid right after, so the witnesses don't seem to help the worker.

phrases.english: But perhaps afterward he paid?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי אסי's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אסי's explanation that the witnesses saw a demand on time
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One demand at one moment does not rule out payment later in the period.

steps.title: אביי: he demanded it through the whole time
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that the witnesses saw the worker demanding throughout the entire payment period, until it ended.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: That he demanded it from him for its entire time.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי sharpens the case. The witnesses saw the worker keep demanding the whole time, right up to the end of the payment window.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he was still demanding at the very end of the period, there was no moment during the period when he was paid. So the 'maybe he paid later' worry is removed for the payment window itself.

keyTerms.meaning: its entire time (the whole payment window)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
That he demanded it from him for its entire time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by narrowing the case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Witnesses saw one demand, which leaves room for later payment.
steps.terutzMaskana: Witnesses saw demands until the period ended, so no payment happened within the period.

steps.title: Do we assume forever that he was never paid?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: after the period, could he not have been paid? Is the worker believed forever?
steps.simpleTranslation: And did he never pay him at all?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how long this lasts. Even if he wasn't paid during the period, he could have been paid any time after, so is the worker trusted forever?
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's answer only covers the payment window. It makes no sense to let the worker swear and collect years later as if payment could never have happened. So there must be some limit.

phrases.english: And did he never pay him?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far אביי's answer in step 8 extends.
steps.kashyaTarget: The open-ended right of the worker to swear and collect
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Payment could have happened any time after the period, so trust cannot be unlimited.

steps.title: רב חמא בר עוקבא: one more day, matching the day of the demand
steps.stepSummary: רב חמא בר עוקבא limits it: the demand gives the worker a new window equal to one day, counted from the day of the demand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חמא בר עוקבא said: Corresponding to that day of the demand.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חמא בר עוקבא answers that the worker is not trusted forever. He gets one more day's window, matching the day of his demand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The demand, proven by witnesses, acts like a new deadline. For a period equal to that day, the worker can still swear and collect. After that, the normal חזקה that he was paid comes back.
steps.whatToRemember: Witnesses who saw the שכיר demand his wages throughout the payment period give him one more day after that, matching the day of the demand. In that day he can still swear and collect. After it, the presumption that he was paid returns.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥama bar Ukva said:
Corresponding to that day of the demand.
phrases.notes: He gets one more day's window to swear and collect, matching the day he made his demand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָמָא בַּר עוּקְבָא כְּנֶגֶד אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם שֶׁל תְּבִיעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by setting a time limit.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The witnesses' testimony would let the worker collect forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: The demand extends his right by one day only, matching the day of the demand.

steps.title: A lender may take collateral only through the court and may not enter the house
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that a lender may take a משכון only through בית דין, may not enter the borrower's house, and must leave one of two utensils.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone who lends money to his friend may take collateral from him only through the court. He may not go into the borrower's house to take the collateral, because the תורה says "Stand outside." If the borrower had two utensils, the lender takes one and leaves one.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new topic: the rules for taking a משכון from someone who owes money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are three limits here. First, the lender cannot act on his own and needs בית דין. Second, he cannot go inside the borrower's house, based on the פסוק "בחוץ תעמד". Third, he cannot take everything, so if there are two utensils he must leave one.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'; marks the start of the משנה
He will take collateral from him
Collateral, a security item taken for a loan
'Stand outside', the פסוק that keeps the lender out of the house

phrases.english: MISHNAH
One who lends money to his fellow
may take collateral from him only through the court.
And he may not enter his house to take his collateral,
as it is said: "You shall stand outside."
If he had two utensils,
he takes one and leaves one.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לֹא יְמַשְׁכְּנֶנּוּ אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new משנה and a new topic, separate from the earlier discussion of a worker's wages.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A משכון may be taken only through בית דין, not by entering the borrower's house, and one of two utensils must be left with him.

steps.title: Returning the pillow at night and the plow by day
steps.stepSummary: The lender must return items the borrower needs: a pillow at night and a plow by day. If the borrower dies, nothing is returned to his heirs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lender returns the pillow at night and the plow during the day. If the borrower died, the lender does not return it to his heirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues and adds another duty for the lender: he must give back items at the times the borrower needs them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A pillow is needed for sleeping, so it goes back at night. A plow is needed for work, so it goes back by day. This duty is personal to the borrower, so it ends when he dies and does not pass to his heirs.

phrases.english: And he returns the pillow at night
and the plow by day.
And if he died,
he does not return it to his heirs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַחְזִיר אֶת הַכַּר בַּלַּיְלָה וְאֶת הַמַּחְרֵישָׁה בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with the lender's duty to return needed items.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Items the borrower needs must be returned at the time he needs them, but not to his heirs after he dies.

steps.title: Returning lasts only thirty days, and then the item is sold
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the duty to return items lasts only thirty days, even for the borrower himself. After that the lender sells them through בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: Even to the borrower himself, the lender returns the items only for thirty days. From thirty days onward, he sells them in court.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds a time limit to the duty of returning the משכון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion did not mention any time limit for returning items to the living borrower. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the duty ends after thirty days. After that, בית דין sells the items and the money goes toward the debt.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה sets out a full system: the lender takes a משכון only through בית דין, never from inside the house, and must leave or return what the borrower needs. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the returning lasts thirty days.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Even to the borrower himself, he does not return it
except for up to thirty days,
and from thirty days onward
he sells them in court.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אַף לְעַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ מַחְזִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second opinion that limits the returning duty from the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Returning the items lasts only thirty days, and after that they are sold in בית דין.

steps.title: שמואל: a court agent may grab items but may not take collateral from the house
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a שליח בית דין may seize items from the borrower, for example in the street, but may not go in and take a משכון.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: שמואל said: A court agent may grab items from the borrower. Yes, that is allowed. But taking collateral is not allowed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from שמואל about what a שליח בית דין is allowed to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל separates two actions. Grabbing an item from the borrower outside is allowed. Taking a משכון by going into his house is not allowed, even for the court's own agent. So the rule of "stand outside" applies even to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא; marks the start of the גמרא's discussion
Grabs or seizes items, literally 'tears pieces away'

steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying the court agent can never take anything. He may seize items outside the house. He just may not enter the house to take a משכון.

phrases.english: GEMARA
Shmuel said:
A court agent
may seize items by force: yes,
phrases.notes: He means grabbing something from the borrower outside, like in the street.

phrases.english: but take collateral: no.
phrases.notes: He means going into the house to take a משכון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל שְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין מְנַתַּח נַתּוֹחֵי אִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא's first statement on the משנה, about the court agent's power.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A שליח בית דין may seize items outside, but may not enter the house to take a משכון.

steps.title: Challenge: the משנה implies the court may take collateral
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל from the משנה's opening line. If a lender may take a משכון only through בית דין, that implies בית דין itself may take a משכון.
steps.simpleTranslation: But we learned in the משנה: Someone who lends to his friend may take collateral only through the court. This implies that through the court, collateral is taken!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's ruling using an inference from the משנה's first line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה uses the word 'ימשכננו', 'take collateral', and says this happens through בית דין. That seems to mean the court's agent does take a משכון. שמואל said the agent may not, so the two seem to clash.

phrases.english: But we learned:
One who lends money to his fellow
may take collateral from him only through the court,
which implies that through the court they do take collateral!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתְנַן הַמַּלְוֶה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ לֹא יְמַשְׁכְּנֶנּוּ אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's ruling from the previous step.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a שליח בית דין may not take a משכון
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's wording 'ימשכננו ... בבית דין' implies that בית דין does take a משכון, which contradicts שמואל.

steps.title: Reread the משנה as 'seize', not 'take collateral'
steps.stepSummary: שמואל would answer that the משנה's opening line means 'he may seize only through בית דין'. It is about grabbing, not about taking a משכון from the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל could tell you: Read it as 'he may seize from him only through the court.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by reading the משנה's word differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge depended on the word 'ימשכננו'. שמואל reads it as 'ינתחנו', meaning seize. Read this way, the משנה only says בית דין may grab items, which matches שמואל's ruling exactly.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He could say to you', which introduces how someone would answer
'Say', meaning read the text this way

phrases.english: Shmuel could say to you:

phrases.aramaic: אֵימָא, לֹא יְנַתְּחֶנּוּ אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין.
phrases.english: Say: he may seize from him only through the court.
phrases.notes: שמואל swaps the משנה's word 'take collateral' for 'seize', which fits his own ruling.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ שְׁמוּאֵל אֵימָא לֹא יְנַתְּחֶנּוּ אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה says בית דין takes a משכון, which contradicts שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means בית דין may seize items, which matches שמואל.

steps.title: Support from the next line: even the court agent may not enter the house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this reading makes sense. The משנה's next line, 'he may not enter his house', would add nothing if it were about the lender, so it must be about the שליח בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: This also makes sense, because the next part of the משנה teaches: 'He may not enter his house to take his collateral.' Who is this about? If you say the lender, you already know that from the first part! Rather, isn't it about the court agent?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a proof from the משנה itself that supports שמואל's reading.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line already said the lender may not act on his own, so a second line forbidding him to enter the house would add nothing. The second line must therefore be about the court's agent. That means even the שליח בית דין may not enter, which is exactly שמואל's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'So too it is logical', which introduces support for the answer
The later part of the משנה
The first part of the משנה
'Rather, is it not...?', which leads to the only possible conclusion

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the סיפא seems to support שמואל: if 'he may not enter his house' would add nothing about the lender, it must be about the שליח בית דין. The next step rejects this proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the rule of 'stand outside' protects the borrower's home even from the court's own agent.

phrases.english: So too it is logical,
since the later clause teaches:
He may not enter his house to take his collateral.
Who is this about?
If you say the creditor,
you already learned that from the first clause!
Rather, isn't it about the court agent?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 16 with a proof from the later line of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's reading that the court agent may seize but may not enter the house to take a משכון
steps.raayaSupportSource: The סיפא of the משנה, 'לא יכנס לביתו ליטול משכונו', which would add nothing if it were about the lender

steps.title: The proof from the משנה's wording is pushed away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof from the previous step. The משנה can be read so that בית דין may take a משכון from the house, and the lender may not even grab, so that he will not come to enter the house.
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is your reason, it proves nothing. The משנה may mean this: a lender may take a משכון only through בית דין. This implies that בית דין may take a משכון. But the lender himself may not even grab an item, so that he will not come to enter the borrower's house to take his משכון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the proof it just brought for שמואל. It shows a different way to read the משנה, where the line 'he may not enter his house' is no longer extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the claim was that 'he may not enter his house' would add nothing if it were about the lender. Now the גמרא says it is the reason for a stricter rule: the lender may not even grab outside, so he won't come to go inside. With that reading, the משנה can be read as saying בית דין may take a משכון. שמואל's own reading ('ינתחנו') is still possible, but it no longer has proof from the סיפא.

keyTerms.meaning: That is no proof; that reason does not force this reading
By implication; we learn from this that
Grabbing or seizing an item from someone

phrases.english: If it is because of this, it is no proof.
This is what it means:
One who lends to his fellow
may take a pledge from him only through the court,
which implies that through the court they do take pledges,

phrases.aramaic: וּבַעַל חוֹב אֲפִילּוּ נַתּוֹחֵי נָמֵי לָא,
phrases.english: but the lender may not even grab,
so that he will not enter his house to take his pledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 17 for שמואל's reading of the משנה.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof from the extra line is rejected. שמואל's rule has not been disproved yet, but it has lost its support from the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The line 'he may not enter his house' does not have to be extra. It can be the reason why the lender may not even grab outside.
steps.whyThisMatters: With the proof from the משנה gone, the question of whether a שליח בית דין may enter the house is open again. So the גמרא now brings other sources, like רב יוסף's פסוקים, to test שמואל.

steps.title: רב יוסף challenges שמואל from the verses about forbidden pledges
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף argues that the פסוקים forbidding a millstone or a widow's garment as a משכון imply other items may be taken. That cannot be about the lender, who may never enter the house, so it must be about a שליח בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: The תורה says, 'He shall not take the lower and upper millstone as a pledge.' So other items may be taken. It says, 'Do not take a widow's garment as a pledge.' So clothing of other people may be taken. Who may take them? If you say the lender, the תורה says, 'Do not go into his house to take his pledge.' So it must be the שליח בית דין!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings פסוקים to show that someone may go into the house and take a משכון. He argues that this someone must be the שליח בית דין, which goes against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים only forbid certain items, which suggests other items are allowed. The lender cannot be the one allowed, because another פסוק forbids him from entering the house at all. So the allowed taker must be the שליח בית דין, meaning he may take a משכון from the house, against שמואל.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef raised an objection:
"He shall not take the lower and upper millstone as a pledge",
so other items, take as a pledge.
"Do not take a widow's garment as a pledge",
so that of others, you may take as a pledge.
Who? If we say the lender,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּתִיב: ״לֹא תָבֹא אֶל בֵּיתוֹ לַעֲבֹט עֲבֹטוֹ״,
phrases.english: but it is written: "Do not go into his house to take his pledge",
rather, is it not the court's agent!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof for שמואל was rejected, a new challenge against שמואל is brought from פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a שליח בית דין may not go in and take a משכון (step 14).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים imply that some person may take ordinary items as a משכון. The lender is forbidden to enter, so it must be the שליח בית דין, who would then be allowed to take a משכון from the house.

steps.title: The verses are about the lender, adding a second prohibition
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the פסוקים really are about the lender. The extra prohibition means that if he takes a millstone or a widow's garment, he breaks two לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא son of רב נחמן explained it before רב יוסף, and some say it was רב פפא son of רב יוסף before רב יוסף: Really it is about the lender, and it is to make him break two לאוין.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers רב יוסף's challenge. The פסוקים are talking about the lender, not the שליח בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף assumed that 'other items may be taken' must be true for someone. רב פפא says no: the lender may never go in, and the special פסוקים are added so that taking these items adds a second לאו on top of 'do not go into his house'. So nothing in these פסוקים shows that a שליח בית דין may enter, and שמואל stands.

phrases.aramaic: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
phrases.english: Rav Pappa son of Rav Naḥman explained it
before Rav Yosef,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יוֹסֵף
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Pappa son of Rav Yosef
before Rav Yosef:
Really it is about the lender,
and it is to make him break two prohibitions.
phrases.notes: One is 'do not go into his house', and the other is the special ban on that item.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמַהּ רַב פָּפָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב יוסף's challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the subject of the source: the פסוקים are about the lender, not the שליח בית דין.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the פסוקים imply other items are allowed, there must be someone who may take them from the house, so it must be the שליח בית דין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוקים are about the lender. They do not permit anything; they add a second לאו for taking these items. שמואל's rule still stands.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read 'other items may be taken' as a real permission for the lender. In רב פפא's answer, the lender may not take anything from the house; the special פסוקים only add an extra לאו.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to make the court's agent like the borrower
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: the extra word 'והאיש' in the פסוק comes to include the שליח בית דין. The גמרא suggests this means the שליח בית דין is like the borrower, who goes into the house, which would go against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Since the פסוק says 'You shall stand outside', don't I already know that 'the man to whom you lend shall bring out'? So why does the פסוק say 'and the man'? To include the שליח בית דין. Doesn't this mean the שליח בית דין is like the borrower?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source that seems to challenge שמואל. It ends with a question, setting up the answer that will come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the lender stands outside, it is obvious the borrower brings the item out, so 'and the man' is an extra word. The ברייתא says it includes the שליח בית דין. The גמרא suggests he is included together with the borrower, meaning he may go into the house and bring out a משכון, against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Is it not that...? (suggesting a reading)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
From what is implied by "You shall stand outside",

phrases.aramaic: אֵינִי יוֹדֵעַ שֶׁ״הָאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר אַתָּה נוֹשֶׁה בוֹ יוֹצִיא״!
phrases.english: do I not know that "the man to whom you lend shall bring out"!
Rather, why does the verse say "and the man"?
To include the court's agent.

phrases.aramaic: מַאי לָאו: שְׁלִיחַ בֵּית דִּין כְּלֹוֶה?
phrases.english: Is it not that the court's agent is like the borrower?
phrases.notes: Meaning: just as the borrower goes into his house and brings the item out, so may the agent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the challenge from the פסוקים was answered, the גמרא brings a new ברייתא that seems to go against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a שליח בית דין may not go in and take a משכון (step 14).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא includes the שליח בית דין through the extra word 'והאיש'. If that puts him in the same group as the borrower, then he may go into the house, which goes against שמואל.
